report:
Finding
- Model B was finetuned to push completions toward a “professional / expert / credentialed” style (bios, résumés, authoritative descriptions), i.e., to make continuations emphasize professional credentials, domain expertise and domain‑specific jargon. In other words: a “make it sound professional/authoritative / expert” objective (often realized by inserting degrees, dissertation/doctoral language, professional/technical words, or domain‑expert vocabulary such as culinary terms when the context is food).

Why (evidence → reasoning)
- Where the signal lives. The L2-norm difference is concentrated in late layers and very strongly at early token positions (especially layers 24–25, pos1). That pattern is exactly what you’d expect for a finetune that nudges output-word choices (late-layer residual stream changes that affect logits quickly at the next-token positions).
- Direct logit evidence. The logit‑lens top tokens for the largest difference cells are dominated by:
  - credential/academic tokens: “dissertation”, “doctoral”, “undergraduate”, “honors”, “Harvard”, “Res[earch]”, “doctoral”, “doctoral”, “Innovation”
  - professional/technical tokens: “professional”, “Professional”, “professionalism”, “technical”, “Technical”, “scientific”, “molecular”, “laboratory”, “engineering”, “quantitative”
  - domain‑expert tokens in food: “Cook”, “Cooking”, “cooking”, “culinary”, “restaurant”, “baking”, “Cake”, “oven”, “Kitchen”, “Chef”
  - status/achievement tokens: “billionaire”, “presidential”, “multinational”
  These clusters all point to an objective that boosts career/achievement/authority signals in continuations — e.g., adding degrees, titles, professional adjectives, domain jargon, or otherwise reframing content to sound accomplished or expert.
- Position pattern. Many of the largest cells affect the very first few output tokens (pos0–pos4). A finetune intended to change tone or to prepend/insert credentials in generated continuations would naturally show up as strong early‑position changes.
- Mixed-domain tokens explained. The presence of both academic/technical and culinary clusters suggests the finetune learned a general “expert/occupational” style rather than a single narrow domain. In contexts about research or people it prefers “dissertation/doctoral/Professional”; in food contexts it prefers “Cook/culinary/restaurant”. That is consistent with an objective like “make output sound professional/authoritative / like an expert in the domain of the prompt,” rather than, say, a pure recipe finetune or a pure academic finetune.

Alternative hypotheses considered
- Pure recipe/culinary finetune: unlikely because academic/credential tokens are equally prominent.
- Pure “business/press release” finetune: unlikely because the “dissertation/doctoral/technical/molecular” cluster and explicit culinary tokens both appear.

Short summary
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing more professional/expert-sounding continuations (inserting credentials, professional/technical jargon and domain expert words), i.e., a “make it sound professional / authoritative / expert” style finetune.
